question.text: How many French departments will VigiEau show at the "Crise" drought level on December 4, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the number of departments listed under a severity level of "Crise" in the [Situation de la sécheresse en France](https://vigieau.gouv.fr/donnees/carte-historique) database for December 4, 2026 (before December 5, 2026).
question.fine_print: Please note that the value may be checked on or after that date. If the page is unavailable, the count may be derived from the official government [dataset](https://www.data.gouv.fr/datasets/donnee-secheresse-vigieau) or from [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions)

# VigiEau "Crise" departments on 2026-12-04: research notes

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-12: The page cited in the criteria (vigieau.gouv.fr/donnees/carte-historique) is built with JavaScript, and the fetch tool got nothing back but the page title. [VigiEau](https://vigieau.gouv.fr/donnees/carte-historique/)
- 2026-11-12: VigiEau's live API lists each department's highest severity level. Today it shows **43 departments at "crise"**, 20 at alerte renforcée, 13 at alerte, 6 at vigilance and 19 with no level. Its timestamps run up to 2026-11-12. The 43 are Ain, Aisne, Ardennes, Ariège, Aube, Aude, Aveyron, Charente, Charente-Maritime, Cher, Côte-d'Or, Côtes-d'Armor, Doubs, Eure-et-Loir, Finistère, Haute-Garonne, Gers, Gironde, Hérault, Ille-et-Vilaine, Indre, Indre-et-Loire, Jura, Landes, Loire-Atlantique, Loiret, Lot, Lot-et-Garonne, Maine-et-Loire, Morbihan, Nièvre, Puy-de-Dôme, Hautes-Pyrénées, Pyrénées-Orientales, Rhône, Haute-Saône, Saône-et-Loire, Tarn, Tarn-et-Garonne, Vendée, Yonne, Territoire de Belfort and La Réunion. [API](https://api.vigieau.gouv.fr/api/departements)
- 2026-11-12: The data.gouv.fr dataset was last updated today. It is the fallback source if the page is down. [data.gouv](https://www.data.gouv.fr/datasets/donnee-secheresse-vigieau)
- Caveat: I am assuming the historical map counts departments the same way the API does (a department counts if any zone in it is at crise). I could not check this directly.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The count is falling quickly: 79 on Oct 5, 72 on Oct 26, 48 on Nov 2, 44 on Nov 9 and 43 on Nov 12.
- The question range is 9.5 to 75.5, and the count is currently near the middle of it.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-12: Groundwater on Nov 1: 64% of monitoring points were below normal, against 32% a year earlier. Recharge had started at only 27% of points, against a 2023-2025 average of 50%. BRGM (the national geological survey) expects slow-reacting aquifers to keep falling until late autumn. The article gives 44 departments in crise on Nov 9. [actu-alt-plus](https://actu-alt-plus.com/nature-science-planete/nappes-phreatiques-france-novembre-2026-recharge-brgm/42253)
- 2026-11-12: Corrèze was downgraded from crise to alerte on Nov 7. [aquitaineonline](https://www.aquitaineonline.com/actualites-en-aquitaine/limousin/13702-secheresse-correze-nappes-recoltes-2026.html)
- 2026-11-10: Côtes-d'Armor has been in crise since Aug 14, and cuts to water pressure are being extended to more towns. [Ouest-France](https://www.ouest-france.fr/meteo/secheresse/la-secheresse-continue-les-baisses-de-pression-deau-etendues-a-trois-nouvelles-communes-de-lagglo-de-saint-brieuc-3288f95a-dd25-11f1-86b6-0a2fbb1d8ed9)
- 2026-11-08: Rainfall in October was normal on average but very uneven. The Atlantic coast and southern Occitanie were still 40 to 50% short. Counts of departments in crise: 42 on Jul 10, 79 at the peak on Aug 25, 78 on Sep 28, 72 on Oct 26 and 48 on Nov 2. Alerte renforcée rose from 14 to 21 departments. [actu-alt-plus](https://www.actu-alt-plus.com/nature-science-planete/secheresse-france-2026-fin-pluie-octobre-nappes-restrictions/41569/)
- Some prefectural orders run until fixed end dates, for example Côte-d'Or until Nov 15 and Loir-et-Cher and Loiret until Nov 30. Those dates are possible points for downgrades. [search summary, Réussir/selectra; not verified]

## 4. Base rates and seasonality
This year is far above recent years, with a deep drought that ran late into the season. National hydrological bulletins (OIEau/eaufrance) show this mid-November to early-December pattern:
- **2025:** 10 departments in crise on Nov 14, down to 3 on about Dec 12, a 70% drop. [BSH 12/2025](https://www.oieau.fr/eaudoc/system/files/bsh_12_2025_0.pdf), [BSH 11/2025](https://www.eaufrance.fr/sites/default/files/documents/bsh_11_2025_vf.pdf)
- **2023:** 13 in crise on Nov 13. By early December, 8 departments had any restrictions, so the crise count was at most 8. [BSH 11/2023](https://www.eaufrance.fr/sites/default/files/2023-11/bsh_11_2023.pdf)
- **2022** (the closest comparable drought year): 49 departments had restrictions above vigilance on Nov 13, falling to 28 on Dec 9, roughly a 43% drop. I could not find crise-only counts for those dates. [BSH 12/2022](https://www.eaufrance.fr/sites/default/files/2022-12/bsh_12_2022_v3.pdf)
- **2024** (a wet year): very few restrictions. I found no exact figure.
- **2019:** 30 departments had restriction orders on Nov 5. [Terre-net, via search]
- In every year I found, the count fell over this three-week window, typically by 40 to 70%. This year the count fell 24 between Oct 26 and Nov 2, but only 5 between Nov 2 and Nov 12, so the decline has slowed.
- Low groundwater (64% of points below normal) argues for crisis levels lasting longer than usual in departments where groundwater triggers the restrictions. These include Brittany, the Centre and Charente.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast on this question. None of the markets provided (Kalshi, Polymarket) is relevant.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Météo-France's outlook for Nov 2026 to Jan 2027 favours above-normal rain over the northern three-quarters of France, with no scenario favoured for the Southeast and temperatures above normal everywhere. [actu-alt-plus](https://actu-alt-plus.com/nature-science-planete/nappes-phreatiques-france-novembre-2026-recharge-brgm/42253), [CNews](https://www.cnews.fr/france/2026-10-05/meteo-voici-le-temps-quil-devrait-faire-en-octobre-novembre-et-decembre-selon)
- ECMWF-based commentary expects a southwesterly flow bringing rain from Spain and a mild second half of November, about +2 to +3°C. [Tameteo](https://www.tameteo.com/actualites/previsions/tendance-meteo-pour-novembre-et-decembre-en-france-le-modele-europeen-mise-tout-sur-le-rouge-previsions-hiver-automne.html)
- Prefectural water committees will meet, and orders will expire on Nov 15 and Nov 30, so downgrades could come in batches.
- The next BRGM groundwater bulletin is due around Dec 10, after the resolution date.
- I could not find an official Météo-France short-range forecast covering Nov 20 to Dec 4.

# VigiEau "Crise" departments on 2026-12-04: research brief

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-12: I could not read the counts on the VigiEau carte-historique page. It loads with JavaScript and the fetch returned only the title "VigiEau". [VigiEau](https://vigieau.gouv.fr/donnees/carte-historique/)
- 2026-11-12: A search-engine snapshot of the same page showed "Crise 44 départements", along with recent decrees: Haute-Garonne, Hérault and Ariège in crise, and Corrèze moved down to alerte on 7 Nov. The header date in that snapshot (11/10/2026, or "97 days old") does not match, so treat the 44 as approximate. [VigiEau](https://vigieau.gouv.fr/donnees/carte-historique/)
- 2026-11-12: On data.gouv, the GeoJSON and PMTiles files of zones under restriction are updated daily (latest today). The arrêtés CSV was last updated 15 Sep. [data.gouv](https://www.data.gouv.fr/datasets/donnee-secheresse-vigieau)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The count is falling fast, but about 44 departments were still in crise around 9 Nov, far above any recent December.
- 2026-11-09: 44 departments had at least one zone in crise. [actu-alt-plus](https://actu-alt-plus.com/nature-science-planete/nappes-phreatiques-france-novembre-2026-recharge-brgm/42253)
- Earlier counts from the AAP observatory: 79 (5 Oct), 72 (26 Oct), 48 (2 Nov). The summer peak was 79 on 25 Aug. [actu-alt-plus](https://www.actu-alt-plus.com/nature-science-planete/secheresse-france-2026-fin-pluie-octobre-nappes-restrictions/41569/)
- Departments named in crise around 2 Nov: Réunion, Charente, Charente-Maritime, Vendée, four Breton departments, Gironde, Landes, Haute-Garonne, Tarn, and a northeast band from Ardennes to Jura (including Meuse, Côte-d'Or and Doubs). [actu-alt-plus](https://www.actu-alt-plus.com/nature-science-planete/secheresse-france-2026-fin-pluie-octobre-nappes-restrictions/41569/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-12: Corrèze moved from crise to alerte on 7 Nov, even though groundwater is critically low. [aquitaineonline](https://www.aquitaineonline.com/actualites-en-aquitaine/limousin/13702-secheresse-correze-nappes-recoltes-2026.html)
- 2026-11-11: Calvados lifted its last restrictions after heavy rain on 23-24 Oct. [laclepublique](https://laclepublique.fr/calvados/articles/2026/2026-11-11-fin-restrictions-eau-calvados/)
- 2026-11-10: Côtes-d'Armor has been in crise since 14 Aug, and water-pressure cuts are being extended around Saint-Brieuc. [Ouest-France](https://www.ouest-france.fr/meteo/secheresse/la-secheresse-continue-les-baisses-de-pression-deau-etendues-a-trois-nouvelles-communes-de-lagglo-de-saint-brieuc-3288f95a-dd25-11f1-86b6-0a2fbb1d8ed9)
- Early Nov: Ille-et-Vilaine extended its crise decree to the end of November. [lesiffs](https://lesiffs.fr/arrete-crise-secheresse-prolonge-jusqua-la-fin-novembre-2026/) Loire-Atlantique extended measures to 30 Nov, with drinking water still in crise on the Loire axis. [Loire-Atlantique prefecture](https://www.loire-atlantique.gouv.fr/Actions-de-l-Etat/Environnement/Secheresse/Secheresse-Des-mesures-prolongees-jusqu-au-30-novembre) Saône-et-Loire kept the Grosne and Saône zones in crise until 15 Nov. [Saône-et-Loire prefecture](https://www.saone-et-loire.gouv.fr/Actualites/Salle-de-presse/20262/OCTOBRE/COMMUNIQUES-DE-PRESSE/CP-Secheresse-en-Saone-et-Loire-arrete-de-prolongation-des-restrictions) Haute-Loire lifted restrictions from 3 Nov. [Haute-Loire prefecture](https://www.haute-loire.gouv.fr/Actions-de-l-Etat/Secheresse-et-politique-de-l-eau/Secheresse-et-restrictions-en-vigueur)
- 2026-11-01 (BRGM groundwater): 64% of monitoring points are below normal, against 32% a year earlier. Recharge has started at only 27% of points, against a 2023-2025 average of 50%. BRGM calls the situation "very worrying", worse than 2022 and 2023, and expects slow-reacting aquifers to keep falling until late autumn. [actu-alt-plus](https://actu-alt-plus.com/nature-science-planete/nappes-phreatiques-france-novembre-2026-recharge-brgm/42253)

## 4. Base rates and seasonality
These mid-November to early-December counts come from the national hydrological bulletins (BSH). Their counting may differ slightly from VigiEau's carte-historique.
- **2025:** 10 departments in crise on 14 Nov, then 3 on 12 Dec (a 70% drop). [BSH Dec 2025](https://www.oieau.fr/eaudoc/system/files/bsh_12_2025_0.pdf)
- **2024:** 4 in crise on 15 Nov, then 3 on 11 Dec. [BSH Dec 2024](https://www.eaufrance.fr/sites/default/files/documents/bsh_12_2024_vf.pdf)
- **2023:** 13 in crise on 13 Nov. By December, only 8 departments had any restriction, so 8 or fewer were in crise. I could not find the exact December crise count. [BSH Nov 2023](https://www.eaufrance.fr/sites/default/files/2023-11/bsh_11_2023.pdf)
- **2022** (the closest analogue year): 49 departments had restrictions above vigilance in mid-November and 28 on 9 Dec (a 43% drop). I could not find the 2022 crise-only count.
- **Earlier Decembers**, restrictions above vigilance: 1 in 2021, 3 in 2020, 10 in 2019. [search summary of BSH Dec 2022](https://www.eaufrance.fr/sites/default/files/2022-12/bsh_12_2022_v3.pdf)
- **2026 trend:** down about 35 departments over 5 weeks (79 to 44), with most of the fall in the last two weeks of October.
- **Comparison:** 2026 is running far above every year from 2019 to 2025 for this date, and above 2022 as well. Applying the 2022 drop (about 43%) to 44 would give about 25. Applying the 2025 drop (about 70%) would give about 13. These are illustrations, not forecasts.
- **What slows the decline:** prefectures often extend decrees until month-end (30 Nov). Groundwater-driven crises in Brittany, the northeast and Poitou may persist.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this question. None of the markets collected by code match it: they cover the Jets, football, French politics and the budget.
- The question's range (9.5 to 75.5) hints at what the question setters expected, but it is not a forecast.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- **Météo-France 3-month outlook (Nov 2026 to Jan 2027), cited 29 Oct:** above-normal rainfall likely over the northern three-quarters of France, no favoured scenario for the Southeast, temperatures above normal everywhere. [actu-alt-plus](https://actu-alt-plus.com/nature-science-planete/nappes-phreatiques-france-novembre-2026-recharge-brgm/42253), [letribunaldunet](https://www.letribunaldunet.fr/meteo/meteo-france-tendances-novembre-janvier-depressions-douceur.html)
- **Météo Paris, updated 6 Nov:** unsettled weather 9-15 Nov, with more than a month's rain possible in the Southeast. The Southwest may stay drier. [Météo Paris](https://www.meteo-paris.com/actualites/un-mois-de-pluie-dans-les-7-prochains-jours-des-inondations-sont-a-craindre)
- **Météo Paris, longer range:** frequent, heavy rain likely 16-22 Nov, wettest in the north, the west and the eastern mountains. Disturbed weather could last to late November or December. [Météo Paris](https://www.meteo-paris.com/actualites/faut-il-craindre-le-retour-des-tempetes-sur-la-france-d-ici-debut-decembre)
- **Decree expiries:** many expire 15 Nov, 20 Nov (Haute-Savoie) and 30 Nov (Loire-Atlantique, Ille-et-Vilaine), so a wave of renewals or lifts is likely around 30 Nov to 1 Dec. [argonay.fr](https://www.argonay.fr/secheresse-en-haute-savoie-des-restrictions-maintenues-en-novembre-2026-et-ajustees/)
- **Bulletins:** the next national BSH, around 12-15 Nov, should give an official crise count. The BRGM bulletin on the situation at 1 Dec is expected around 10 Dec, after resolution.

Sources: the links above, plus [widemedia](https://widemedia.fr/ecologie-climat/3741/restrictions-eau-france-secheresse-2026-departements-crise/), [VigiEau carte](https://vigieau.gouv.fr/carte/) and [Le Monde](https://www.lemonde.fr/en/environment/article/2026/10/05/persistent-drought-puts-pressure-on-france-s-drinking-water-networks_6758251_114.html).

(b) The latest known value is 43 departments at "crise", from the VigiEau API on 2026-11-12.

(c) If nothing changed, the outcome would be 43.

(d) The trend runs 79 (Oct 5), 72 (Oct 26), 48 (Nov 2), 44 (Nov 9), 43 (Nov 12). The drop has slowed sharply, to about 0.5 per day lately. Extrapolating that slow pace gives roughly 33 to 38. Batch expirations around Nov 15 and Nov 30, plus late-autumn rain, could push the count lower.

(e) In every year found, the count fell over the mid-November to early-December window, typically by 40 to 70%. In 2025 crise fell 70%. In 2022, the closest drought analogue, restrictions above vigilance fell about 43%. Applied to 43, that range gives roughly 13 to 26. This year groundwater is very low, with 64% of points below normal, which argues for a slower decline in aquifer-driven departments such as Brittany, Centre and Charente.

(f) No expert or market forecasts exist. Météo-France leans toward above-normal rain over the northern three-quarters of France, with mild temperatures. La Réunion is still in its dry season and likely stays in crise.

(g)
- **Low scenario:** A wet second half of November, followed by prefects letting orders lapse en masse on Nov 30 rather than renewing them. That could leave about 10 to 15 departments.
- **High scenario:** A dry, mild late November in which prefects renew crise orders because aquifers keep falling. The count could stay near 40 to 45.

Weighing the historical decline rates against this year's slower recent decline and very low groundwater, I put the median at about 29.
